newsitem.title: USA: GM output threatened by fire at supplier plant.
newsitem.headline: GM output threatened by fire at supplier plant.

text.p: A Wednesday night fire at a suburban Detroit automotive interior parts plant could affect production at several General Motors Corp. assembly plants, GM said Thursday.

The fire at Textron Automotive's plant in Westland, Mich., destroyed a significant number of plastic headliners and door panels, but the extent of the damage was not yet known, said GM spokesman Thomas Klipstine.
"We will have no problems with any of our facilities today," Klipstine said, adding that production beyond that could depend on how many parts were lost.
Klipstine declined to identify the GM assembly plants that receive parts from the damaged Textron plant, but said they include both car and truck facilities.
A spokesman for Textron Automotive, a unit of Textron Inc. was not immediately available for comment.

Westland Assistant Fire Chief Mark Neal said the blaze broke out in the plant's warehouse section at about 10:45 p.m. EDT Wednesday night, and was largely confined to finished products awaiting shipment.
"There was a large quantity of material that was burned, but there's no real structural damage to the plant," Neal said. "It was pretty well contained by the sprinkler system."
The cause of the blaze was being investigated, Neal said.
